name: Bergen County Division of Senior Services
subject: Free skin cancer talk for Bergen County senior centers
email_body:
Dear Lorraine,

I'm a Rutgers student and co-founder of Every Shade, a student group that gives free 45-minute skin cancer talks for New Jersey seniors. Our talk covers what most health education skips: what skin cancer looks like on every skin tone, and the spots people miss on darker skin (palms, soles, under the nails).

We'd like to offer it at the senior centers, nutrition sites, and programs your office works with in Bergen County, in person or over Zoom on a center's TV. It's free, comes with a large-print handout and a short anonymous before-and-after quiz so you can see what members learned, and we handle the setup. We are students, not doctors, and we say so at every talk; our aim is that people know when and where to get a spot checked, including free and sliding-fee clinics nearby.

Is there a center director or program coordinator you'd suggest we start with, or could we be added to your speakers list for December?

Zain Jaffar

subject: Free health talk for Bethany Baptist Church: skin cancer looks different on darker skin
email_body:
Hello,

My name is Zain Jaffar. I'm a Rutgers student and co-founder of Every Shade, a student group that gives free talks on spotting skin cancer early on every skin tone. Melanoma in Black and brown patients is found later and more often on the palms, soles, and nails, and most health materials never say so.

We'd be honored to offer a free 45-minute talk to the congregation of Bethany Baptist Church, after a service or at a seniors' or health-ministry gathering, in person or on Zoom. We bring a large-print handout, and a short before-and-after quiz so you can see what people learned. We're students, not doctors, and we're clear about that: our aim is that people know what to look for and where to get checked, including free and low-cost options in Essex County.

Is there someone who coordinates health or seniors' programs I should speak with?

Zain Jaffar

name: Islamic Society of Central Jersey (ISCJ)
subject: Free health talk for the Islamic Society of Central Jersey: skin cancer looks different on darker skin
email_body:
Hello,

My name is Zain Jaffar. I'm a Rutgers student and co-founder of Every Shade, a student group that gives free talks on spotting skin cancer early on every skin tone. Melanoma in Black and brown patients is found later and more often on the palms, soles, and nails, and most health materials never say so.

We'd be honored to offer a free 45-minute talk to the congregation of the Islamic Society of Central Jersey, after a service or at a seniors' or health-ministry gathering, in person or on Zoom. We bring a large-print handout (we are also preparing it in Urdu), and a short before-and-after quiz so you can see what people learned. We're students, not doctors, and we're clear about that: our aim is that people know what to look for and where to get checked, including free and low-cost options in Middlesex County.

Is there someone who coordinates health or seniors' programs I should speak with?
